title: Fats buying a Christmas outfit for his Pittsburgh barber's family
summary: Autrey tells how Fats gave his regular barber's wife a coat, the son a coat, and the barber a suit, moving the man to tears.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: What did you -- what do you remember most about Fats, the things that impressed you the most about him?

Let me think of that, let me think. Well, I've seen -- well I thought -- I think it was in Pittsburgh, one thing -- I think the thing I often think about, we'd get into town, and he would need a shave and a haircut. I don't know for what reason, or who called and told him about this man. He called this man. The man came to the hotel, gave him a haircut, a shave, so it lasted for -- I don't know how many years. Each time we would go in and out of Pittsburgh it lasted, several times.

So I happened to be there with him on this particular instance, and at Christmas time, and he needed this man's services, haircut and shave both. At this time he bought this man's wife a winter coat, his son, little boy, must have looked like -- to me -- about 12, 13, and the husband, a suit, and coat. Said Merry Christmas.

To me that's one of the greatest things I had ever seen. The man cried. The man did not expect it. He was a poor man. He had a -- it was a poor family. Now things like that, I think, are worthwhile. Maybe I'm wrong.
Fats was very generous that way, wasn't he?
Very generous, very generous. And I liked that. To me it -- I don't know. Well, maybe I'm an old -- what do you call them? (Laughs.)
Yeah, but I liked it. I felt that was kind of nice.
Did he do things like this quite often?
